abstract.para: Youth Tech Net ANU Hub acknowledges the traditional custodians of the land on which ANU and the Club operate from, the Ngunnawal and Ngambri peoples. We recognise the continuing connection to lands, waters, and communities of all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. We pay our respect to Elders, past and present, and commit to standing with our First Nations People.

section.title: Name
section.simpara: The official name of the club to which this Constitution applies is "Youth Tech Net ANU Hub".

section.title: Interpretation
section.para:
In this Constitution, unless contrary intention appears:
Academic day means a 24-hour period during any day or days that do not fall on a weekend or public holiday, and that fall during a Teaching Period of the Academic Colleges.
ANUSA means the Australian National University Students' Association Inc.
Club means Youth Tech Net ANU Hub.
Executive means the Executive Committee of the Club.
Meeting means a General Meeting, Special General Meeting, or Annual General Meeting of the Club.
Member means any full or associate member of the Club.
Student means any student of the University who retains membership of ANUSA.
University means the Australian National University.

listitem.simpara: Any interpretation of this constitution or the resolution of any dispute under it may be appealed to the ANUSA Clubs Officer. The decision of the ANUSA Clubs Officer may be appealed by the means set out in the constitution and regulations of ANUSA.
The Club is affiliated to ANUSA and anything in this Constitution which is inconsistent with ANUSA's Clubs Regulations and Policies is null and void to the extent of that inconsistency.
The Club must fulfil its obligations under the ANUSA Clubs Regulations and Policies.
The Club is recognised as a University Hub of Youth Tech Net Australia.

section.title: Aims and Objectives
section.para: The aims and objectives of the Club are to:

listitem.simpara: Provide an open discussion forum for students interested in the intersection of society, technology, and technology policy;
Run informational and educational events for members about technology and society issues, such as seminars, workshops, and reading clubs;

Platform student perspectives on technology policy issues by publishing their work on Youth Tech Net's website, which may include white papers, policy briefs, opinion pieces, articles, and research projects;
Facilitate the pursuit of research projects by members.
Full membership is open to all currently enrolled ANU students who have paid the relevant subscription fee.
Associate membership is open to all other persons, subject to approval by the Executive, who have paid the relevant subscription fee.
The subscription fee for full membership is determined by the Executive, but may not be greater than $20 for students, unless the Club applies for an exemption from the ANUSA Clubs Officer.
Membership is valid for the year in which the subscription fee is paid.

Membership may be suspended or withdrawn by a resolution carried by a two-thirds majority of full members present and voting at a General Meeting. Appeals against such a decision may be made as outlined in .

Associate members are ineligible to vote at any General Meeting, may be charged a higher membership fee by the Club, and may be charged a higher fee to attend events staged by the Club, but otherwise are to have the same rights as full members.
A roll recording the name and membership number of all Club members, and the student number of all full members, is to be held and kept up to date by the Executive.
The Club's Executive consists of three members, who are —
the President; and
the Treasurer; and
the Secretary.
The Executive includes such other members as the Club from time to time determines.
All members of the Executive must be either full or associate members, and an absolute majority of the Executive must be full members.
The Executive is to be elected at each Annual General Meeting by a vote involving the full members, but not the associate members, of the Club.

In the event of a dispute between Executive members, or between the Executive and the members of the Club, the President has a duty to make it known to the parties to the dispute that an appeal can be brought to the Clubs Officer for any decision made by the Club's Executive team.
A meeting of the Executive is to be held at least once during each Teaching Period of the Academic year, when and where the Executive sees fit.
The quorum for a meeting of the Executive is the next whole number above half the number of members of the current Executive.
The Executive has the power to fill any vacancy in the Executive that may occur between Annual General Meetings.
The Executive has the power to do all things it believes to be in the best interests of the Club, subject to the provisions of this Constitution and the ANUSA Clubs Regulations and Policies.
Individual members of the Executive are bound by a resolution of a quorate Executive meeting to the extent that the resolution directly relates to their activities as a member of the Executive.
Where all or a majority of the Executive positions are not filled at a general meeting, the Clubs Council may appoint the remaining positions on an interim basis or dissolve the Club.
The Club shall, as soon as is practicable, hold another general meeting at which the positions filled by the Clubs Council shall be filled by election, or dissolve the Club.
Upon failure to elect a majority of Executive positions at the General Meeting referred to in , not inclusive of those filled by Clubs Council, the Club shall be dissolved.

An Annual General Meeting is to be held at least once each year, not more than 14 months after the previous Annual General Meeting, at which the members of the Executive are to be elected, and an Annual Report, statements of income and expenditure, and a current balance sheet are to be presented by the outgoing Executive.
A General Meeting may be convened no more than once during each Teaching Period of the Academic year at the discretion of the Executive.

A Special General Meeting must be called by the Executive within ten academic days of being presented with a petition signed by ten members setting out the purpose for which such a meeting is requested.
A resolution of a quorate General Meeting removing an Executive member from office will be successful if passed by a two-thirds majority.
The quorum for a General Meeting is five members.
Except as set out in , , and of this Constitution, decisions of a General Meeting are by a simple majority of full members present in person who cast a vote.
The Club President must, where possible, Chair, or appoint another Club member to Chair, a General Meeting. Where this is not done, those full members present must elect a Club member to Chair.
The Chair has a deliberative and casting vote.
Any resolution of a quorate General Meeting binds all members of the Executive to the extent that the resolution directly relates to their activities as a member of the Executive.
The assets and income of the Club shall be used only for the promotion of its objectives and no portion may be paid or transferred directly or indirectly to members except as —
bona fide remuneration for services rendered by the members to the Club; or
repayment of expenses incurred on behalf of the Club.
The Club's bank account must —
be only for the use of the Club;
be registered under the Club's name;
have ANUSA's address as the registered address for the bank account;
be a two-to-sign or similar account; and
have exactly three Club executive members (trustees) authorised to operate the account.
The Trustees of the Club are the President, Treasurer, and Secretary.

The Trustees have a legal duty to ensure that Club funds are being used in the best interests of the Club, which is to be viewed from the perspective of the Club as an independent entity, and not from the perspective of members.
Subject to this Constitution, the Executive may by a simple majority at an Executive meeting make or amend Club policies as would assist the convenient conduct of the Club's business.
Policies must be made available to members.

The Club can be dissolved by decision of the current membership at a general meeting, or when the Club ceases to operate due to no members being elected to the Executive positions or appointed by the Clubs Officer.

On dissolution, disaffiliation, or failure to re-affiliate by the end of the first teaching period, any net assets, property, funds or money shall not be distributed among the members but shall become the property of ANUSA and be given or transferred to ANUSA; except for funds sourced by means other than grants from ANUSA in the current and previous calendar year. Such other funds must be donated to a not-for-profit association with objects similar to those of the Club, or to ANUSA.

No amendments to this constitution shall be validly enacted except where the Clubs Council Executive is given notice by email of the amendment at least 5 days prior to the moving of the amendment. The email shall request an interpretation as to whether the proposed amendment will affect the continued eligibility of the Club for affiliation.
This Constitution may be amended by a resolution carried by a two-thirds majority of full members present and voting at a General Meeting.
Notice of proposed amendments must be given to members at least 5 calendar days prior to the General Meeting.
